sections.h2: One government for city and county
sections.html:
Broomfield is a city and a county at once. The two merged on November 15, 2001, which made it Colorado's 64th and newest county. Residents numbered 74,112 in 2020 and about 79,174 by the 2025 estimate.

A single government makes selling less of a runaround. Your tax bill, your recorded deed and any building permit all trace back to Broomfield, so you rarely have to work out which of two offices handles a given question. That also means one set of hours, one phone directory and one place to ask if a document goes missing. Big corporate employers are based here too, and when a transfer lands with little warning, an owner may need to close sooner than a normal listing would allow.

Accepted ways to pay are cash, check, eCheck and credit card. Cards carry a provider fee of 2.50 percent, while an eCheck runs $2.50. Walk-in payments go to the Treasurer at One DesCombes Drive, and the phone line is 303-464-5810.

Ask the Treasurer for this document when you sell. It certifies that the parcel's property taxes are paid, apart from any amounts it lists as still owed, and it shields a purchaser from older delinquent taxes that nobody mentioned. Escrow officers usually order it on their own. When it shows a balance, that sum comes out of your proceeds. More detail is on the Broomfield Treasurer page.

Do not wait for the certificate to learn what you owe. A quick call to the Treasurer, before you agree to any offer, tells you whether a hidden balance exists, and a problem found early is cheaper to fix. Ask for the amount in writing so you can show it to the buyer.

Deeds for Broomfield property are filed with the City and County Clerk and Recorder for a flat $40 plus a $3 surcharge on each document. House Bill 24-1269 created that flat charge, and it began July 1, 2025 for the entire state.

The online index reaches back to November 2001. Anything older may be held by Adams, Boulder, Jefferson or Weld county, the four from which Broomfield was formed. Walk-ins and appointments are open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the office also takes e-recording and mailed documents. Form TD 1000, the Real Property Transfer Declaration, travels with the deed. Because staff are barred from offering legal advice or running a records search for you, the escrow officer typically handles filing. Details are on the Recording page.

Annual precipitation is about 16.1 inches in this cold semi-arid climate. A typical July afternoon reaches 88.7 degrees Fahrenheit, and December nights fall to an average of 18.0. Roofs, painted siding, fences and sprinkler lines absorb that stress. An inspector sent by a lender's buyer will examine each. A buyer paying cash simply builds the wear into the price and leaves the repair work to them.

sections.h2: Which school district is my address in?
sections.html: Boulder Valley, 27J, Weld County RE-8, Jefferson County, St. Vrain Valley and Adams 12 Five Star all reach into Broomfield. Which one applies depends on the street, so confirm yours before describing the schools to a prospective buyer. Inside the city sit two high schools, two middle schools, eight elementary schools, two K to 12 charter schools and four private schools.

The city council is also the board of county commissioners, and the police chief is the county sheriff. Practically, that means one switchboard. Call the Treasurer about money owed on the parcel, the Clerk and Recorder about anything filed against the title, and the building office if you did work on the house and cannot recall whether a permit was pulled.

sections.h2: What a cash purchase leaves out
sections.html:
Financed deals bring an appraisal, a lender's underwriting and frequently a round of repair demands after the buyer's inspection. Any of those can delay closing or reopen the price. A buyer paying cash is spared them. The protective parts remain: a search of the title, the tax certificate and the recorded deed.

Nobody has to wait for a bank to schedule an appraiser or a loan committee to meet. The result is a closing day that fits your plans, whether you must leave fast for a new job or want extra weeks to pack.

Out-of-state heirs usually have the worst of it. Showings, repair visits and utility bills all have to be arranged remotely. A vacant rental raises a similar problem, since the tax dates in February, April and June arrive whether or not anyone lives there, and late penalties grow every month.

If that describes your house, order the Certificate of Taxes Due now, learn what is owed, and choose between a listing and a fast as-is sale before the next due date arrives.

sections.h2: What shows up on the closing statement
sections.html:
Expect to see the recording charge, the state transfer paperwork, the current year's tax split between you and the buyer, and any payoff of a loan or old tax balance. Cards and eChecks are for paying the Treasurer directly, so they will not appear here, but the Certificate of Taxes Due result will.

Compare each line with the figures you were quoted. If anything differs, ask the escrow officer to explain it before you sign, not after the deed has been filed.

sections.h2: What do Broomfield sellers commonly face?
sections.html:
Condition and calendar, more than demand, shape most local sales. Examples:

  • a job change or relocation with a date already fixed
  • heirs scattered across several states
  • an aging roof, furnace or water heater
  • a vacant rental, or one with a tenant still in it

Taking a cash offer lets you pick the closing date and sidestep repairs, open houses and a buyer's loan approval. Nothing stops you from weighing it against a listing first.

1. Send us the address and a few details about the house.
  2. We look it over and give you a written offer.
  3. Escrow opens at a title company, which orders the Certificate of Taxes Due.
  4. You sign, the Broomfield Clerk and Recorder files the deed, and the money is released.

Declining at the offer stage costs nothing. If you proceed, have the newest tax statement, payoff paperwork for any loan, and photo identification ready for signing day. Mention any rush to the escrow officer at the start. The officer can say early whether the closing date you want is realistic.

faqs.q: Is Broomfield a city or a county?
faqs.a: Both. Broomfield consolidated into a single city and county on November 15, 2001, and it is the newest county in Colorado.

faqs.q: When do Broomfield property taxes come due?
faqs.a: April 30 for a single full payment. Owners who pay in halves owe the first on February 28 and the second on June 15.

faqs.q: What does a deed recording cost in Broomfield?
faqs.a: A flat $40 plus a $3 surcharge for each document. That rate has applied since July 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Why does a Broomfield sale need a Certificate of Taxes Due?
faqs.a: The Treasurer issues it to confirm that taxes are paid except for amounts listed as owed. It protects the buyer from unlisted older delinquencies, so escrow officers normally order one.

faqs.q: Do I have to repair my Broomfield house before selling?
faqs.a: No, not for a cash buyer who takes it as is. Have a title company or an attorney review any written offer before you sign.
